sources.authority: Primary front identity and relative facade proportions: exactly three repeated front gables, three recessed upper balconies, three ground living-window bays and six distinct door leaves in three pairs. First two bays place the window left and door pair right; right bay mirrors that arrangement. Buff brick, cream recess soffits, dark railings/glazing and warm timber entries; planted walks and bicycle hoops.
sources.limits: No invisible depth, rear facade, unit/stair layout or surveyed roof heights can be derived from this single projection.

sources.authority: Exposed left flank, real balcony recess, two occupied storeys and roof depth relationship. Four visible side-window positions per storey, broad main-roof gable on the left side, common ridge parallel to front, and three front cross-gables intersecting its forward slope.
sources.limits: Perspective lengths and partly occluded garden/ground windows are not metric authority; hidden right/rear details remain inferred.

sources.authority: Topology corroboration only: a continuous transverse main ridge, rear roof plane, three short front cross-ridges and diagonal valley boundaries on the main forward plane. Confirms common rectangular body, three front bays and rear garden.
sources.limits: This remains elevated oblique rather than nadir. Do not use apparent footprint depth, repeated-seam spacing, exact valley nodes, shadow lines or minor planting shifts as surveyed dimensions.

roof_graph.principal_mass: One common two-storey rectangular body under a main gable whose ridge runs parallel to the front facade.
roof_graph.main_roof: Two principal slopes, front and rear, meeting along one transverse ridge; broad main gable closes the left end and an inferred matching right end.
roof_graph.front_cross_gables: Three short ridges perpendicular to the front, one above each balcony bay. Each cross-ridge terminates against the main front slope below the higher main ridge.
roof_graph.junctions: Each cross-gable has two diagonal valley intersections with the main front plane, converging at its ridge termination. Adjacent valleys discharge toward the two bay-divider gutter/downpipe positions and outer front eave ends. Solve continuous watertight plane intersections; do not overlap complete hidden roof fields.
